name: BP+ Data Capture
description: Records a blood-pressure measurement from a Uscom BP+ device directly into a REDCap instrument, and keeps the device's own result XML as a file on the record. An example module, meant to be copied and edited.
$comment-ajax: An ajax action must be declared for the context it is called from, and a
survey respondent is not logged in -- so save-xml is in both lists.
Undeclared, the framework refuses the call and the recording is silently

project-settings.name:
Instrument that carries the BP+ controls
The unique instrument name, not its label. Blank uses bpplus_measurement.

Field-name prefix
The module writes <prefix>sys, <prefix>dia and the rest. Blank uses bpplus_. Change it only if the fields on your instrument are named differently.

Store the raw measurement XML as a file on the record
A full xml result file can exceed the maximum size (65,000) permitted in a text field. Enable to save the full xml result in a File Upload field named <prefix>xml.

What to send the device as the patient ID
The device writes this verbatim into the xml result file which is saved to the SD card (when one is fitted). The patient ID may be useful to reconcile a card full of recordings back to REDCap records. Note a card is removable and nothing on it is access-controlled.

choices.name: The record ID on its own
Nothing -- the device stores no patient ID

project-settings.name:
Custom Patient ID template
Used when 'Custom Patient ID template' is selected above. [record], [instance] and [position] are replaced; everything else is sent as typed. Add :5 to pad record or instance with leading zeros to the specified number of digits. e.g. [record:5] to pad result to 5 digits. [position] is the seated or standing if needed. AOBP results already record bodyPosition in the XML.

Largest recording this project will accept (MB)
Blank uses 1, which is many times the size of any real measurement. Anything larger is refused. A project may lower this to 0.6 but not raise it above 1 — a value outside that range is brought back inside it. The floor is 0.6 because the largest result the hardware can produce, five 180-second determinations, is about 0.53 MB.

Set the device clock from this computer when it is out by more than this many minutes
The device time stamps measurements. The device clock does not track daylight savings changes. Enabling the check ensures the device clock is aligned with the survey host clock. Blank defaults to 5 minutes.

Require the device to be in a particular measurement mode
Refuses to measure when the BP+ reports something else. Leave as Any mode unless the protocol depends on it.

Allow a measurement started on the BP+ itself
Off by default, and leave it off. A measurement begun with the device's own Start button carries no patient ID, belongs to no record, and never reaches REDCap. The module cancels it and tells the operator. Tick this only for a project that watches a device rather than recording from it.

AOBP — Seated: rest before the first reading (seconds)
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default (seated uses 300 s, 30 s, 3 for the three settings). Only used when the BP+ reports AOBP mode.

AOBP — Seated: interval between readings (seconds)
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default.

AOBP — Seated: number of readings
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default.

AOBP — Standing: rest before the first reading (seconds)
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default (standing uses 60 s, 30 s, 2 for the three settings). Only used when the BP+ reports AOBP mode.

AOBP — Standing: interval between readings (seconds)
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default.

AOBP — Standing: number of readings
Blank sends nothing and the device uses its own default.

Show warnings from attempts the device recovered from
The BP+ may automatically retry a measurement and include an alert in the xml result. A retry may subsequently succeed. Turn ON if you want to see the warnings on measurements that succeeded after the retry. The alerts are recorded in the XML even when not displayed.

Log every serial line to the browser console
Troubleshooting only. Every command sent to the BP+ and every line it answers with, which is what a support report needs when a device behaves differently on one site and not another. Off for normal use: it says nothing an operator can act on.

TESTING ONLY — simulated BP+
When enabled, the survey, the file storage and the record can be tested with no BP+ and no cable using measurements from a built-in simulator instead of a real device. Readings are fabricated. The page displays a warning in a red banner, and every record is written with a device id beginning SIMULATED-. Never enable this on a project collecting real data.
